query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a protective coating of aluminum oxide (Al2O3) will enhance the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr at high temperatures.
generation.conditions: High temperature (800 °C), exposure to air for 5 hours
generation.mechanism: The aluminum oxide coating acts as a barrier to prevent oxygen diffusion into the underlying alloy, thereby reducing oxidation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved oxygen resistance compared to untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, with reduced weight loss and oxidation rate during exposure.
generation.boundary: Temperature: 800 °C; Atmosphere: Air; Exposure time: 5 hours; Loading: No mechanical load applied during oxidation test.
generation.uncertainty: The effectiveness of the aluminum oxide coating on equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has not been previously tested.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct an oxidation test comparing weight loss of coated and uncoated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr samples after 5 hours at 800 °C in air.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the weight loss of the coated sample is not significantly less than that of the uncoated sample, the hypothesis is falsified.
